newsitem.title: CUBA: Cuba rules out dialogue with exile leader.
newsitem.headline: Cuba rules out dialogue with exile leader.

text.p: Cuba's news agency Prensa Latina said on Friday rare simultaneous U.S. television interviews of a senior Cuban official and a right-wing Cuban exile leader revealed "unreconcilable positions."
Prensa Latina was giving its version of interviews recorded on Aug. 23 and broadcast on Thursday night by the U.S.-based Spanish language CBS Telenoticias network.

They linked up Ricardo Alarcon, president of Cuba's National Assembly and a member of the ruling Communist Party Politburo, who spoke from Havana, and Jorge Mas Canosa, head of the fiercely anti-communist Cuban American National Foundation, speaking from Miami.

Prensa Latina said the exchange, which touched on controversial themes such as human rights in Cuba and its one-party Communist government, revealed "unreconcilable positions" between the Cuban government and right-wing Cuban exiles that meant dialogue was impossible.
It described the discussion, part of a two-part CBS series on Cuban President Fidel Castro, as a "dialogue of the deaf" and said the programme was "drowned in sensationalism."

"Far from being a debate ... this confirms the unreconcilable antagonism between the two sides, which makes it not only impossible to have a real dialogue but also unrealistic to attempt a real debate," the agency said.

Supporters of Mas Canosa had hailed the interview as an unprecedented debate between a Cuban government figure and a prominent exile opponent. Cuban Foreign Minister Roberto Robaina has said the interview was not a dialogue nor does it signify any kind of recognition by Havana of Mas Canosa.

Prensa Latina mostly serves international clients and the TV interview involving Alarcon and Mas Canosa has not so far been reported inside Cuba by the domestic Cuban press. It was not clear whether it would ever be shown in Cuba.

Prensa Latina quoted Alarcon as saying during the programme that he had expected to be talking with Peruvian novelist and politician Mario Vargas Llosa but found himself confronting Mas Canosa instead. The agency said this gave the impression that Alarcon's participation in the programme was obtained "through deceit" but it did not elaborate.
